capture_machine: Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.3, sase_core_rs default install
comment: Phase 7E (sase-1e.5) regression-floor baseline; updated in Phase 8F when the Python halves of parser_facade, query_facade.parse_query, and agent_scan_facade were deleted, then extended by notification-store migration Phase 7 (sase-1n.7) and query-corpus Phase 6 (sase-1o.6). Surfaces that previously paired Rust against a live Python median now run only the absolute Rust ceiling check (must_beat_python flipped to false) — historical phase7b_python_median_s fields stay so future tooling can still pivot on them. Core anchors are the stable subset Phase 7B recommended: parse_project_bytes (golden + synthetic_200), parse_query parse-only direct, scan_agent_artifacts synthetic 6p/200pp scan_facade, and apply_status_update golden_myproj_pure (must-not-regress-further guard). Notification anchors pin Rust-backed JSONL snapshot, mutation, modal dismiss, and append/rewrite concurrency surfaces from sdd/tales/202604/notification_rust_migration.md Phase 7. Query-corpus Phase 6 anchors the product persistent-corpus query-keystroke route at the mid-size synthetic workload after the Phase 4 gate and Phase 5 TUI routing were verified; the direct one-shot Rust query row remains diagnostic only.

tolerance.comment: Rust median may be up to 40% slower than the Phase 7B captured Rust median before failing. The 40% headroom (above the plan's 25-35% recommendation) covers GitHub-hosted runner variance vs the Phase 7B capture machine; tighten in Phase 7F or later once we have CI history showing the data is stable. The relative 'must_beat_python' check is hardware-independent and runs on the same machine in the same process, so it stays at parity (no slack). Per-anchor overrides are reserved for explicitly documented high-variance anchors and do not weaken the stable anchors.

notification_store.synthetic_5k.notifica.comment: This full-store read-state mutation uses the production JSONL lock/tempfile/rename write path and showed GitHub-hosted runner IO variance at 194856us with a 157549us confirmation while sibling write-heavy notification anchors were also elevated 3-4x. Typical CI medians are near 47500us, so a 3.0x Phase 7B ceiling (~215055us) still leaves roughly a 4.5x detection margin for a real regression and remains the tightest notification-store write gate.

This modal path performs 25 production one-at-a-time persisted dismissals from a loaded 5k inbox and has shown multi-second GitHub-hosted runner IO variance; keep the extra slack local to this anchor while preserving the global 1.4x gate for stable floors.

scan_agent_artifacts.synthetic_6p_200pp..comment: The Phase 7B baseline (~120 ms) predates several intentional agent-scan wire-shape expansions: pending_question.json marker scanning, workspace_dir / agent-meta tag / PDF activity / image paths / workflow-relationship / epic-start fields on agent_meta and done markers. On the 6-project x 200-per-project synthetic each addition increases both serde parsing on the Rust side and per-record Python dataclass hydration. CI, not local host timing, sets this floor: master CI perf-floors runs from 2026-08-13T22:45Z through 2026-08-14T20:56Z, including CI run IDs 31838558537 and 31840230310, produced observed medians from 146.81 ms through 269.78 ms, with run 31840230310 failing the old 2.15x ceiling at 266.26 ms. Use a 2.35x absolute floor (~282 ms), roughly 4.5% above the worst observed CI median, to cover GitHub-hosted runner heterogeneity while preserving the global 1.4x gate for stable anchors. This still catches a real facade regression that pushes the current CI distribution materially beyond the observed envelope. Revisit when Python hydration is pushed across the PyO3 boundary.

evaluate_query_many.synthetic_1000_specs.comment: The Phase 7B / query-corpus capture (66.70us) is not a portable absolute baseline for this microsecond-scale product route; the same-process must_beat_python gate remains the hardware-independent contract. Eight consecutive master CI perf-floors reports (runs 32532695452, 32537985517, 32542973465, 32546975028, 32551370513, 32555295598, 32558460537, 32568874089) measured 178.28-184.36us while still beating live Python by ~29-30x, and a clean local reproduction measured 147.07us. Use a 2.90x absolute floor (~193.44us), roughly 4.9% above the worst hosted median (184.36us in run 32558460537), to cover GitHub-hosted runner heterogeneity while preserving the global 1.4x gate for stable anchors. This still fails a material regression beyond the observed hosted envelope (2x the hosted max is ~368.72us, about 1.9x the new ceiling). Revisit once hosted medians stabilize near a recaptured baseline on current GitHub runners.

anchors.rationale: Phase 8D deleted the Python parser facade half; this anchor now enforces the absolute Rust ceiling only. Captured as a clean ~2.4x Rust win at the smallest realistic input.
Phase 8D deleted the Python parser facade half; this anchor now enforces the absolute Rust ceiling only. Captured as ~1.4x win on a 200-spec synthetic file.

~2.1x Rust win on direct query parsing (no facade/wire overhead). Phase 7B's evaluate_query_many path is intentionally NOT an anchor because it currently regresses (per-call wire conversion dominates).

Product TUI filter route with the Patch corpus cached and query compilation plus Rust evaluation inside the timed loop. Query-corpus Phase 6 measured ~60x faster than the Python batch baseline on synthetic_1000_specs; the 100 and 10000 rows remain in the Phase 6 artifact as supporting evidence, while the direct one-shot Rust row remains a non-product diagnostic.
Phase 8D deleted the Python scan_agent_artifacts walker; this anchor now enforces the absolute Rust ceiling only. Captured as ~1.21x win on the synthetic 6-project x 200-per-project tree.

Must-not-regress-further guard, not a must-beat-python anchor. Phase 7B showed Rust at parity with Python on this golden workload (~5.8 vs ~5.6 us); the synthetic_200_specs version regresses by ~30% but is too noisy to anchor on. This anchor catches the case where Rust suddenly drops below the recorded floor on an absolute-time basis.

Rust-backed snapshot/count load anchor for the deterministic 5k notification corpus. Phase 1 Python median was 12.700 ms; Phase 7 Rust median was 13.190 ms on this workspace, so this is an absolute ceiling guard rather than a must-beat-python gate.

Rust-backed one-at-a-time dismiss burst over the deterministic 5k corpus. Phase 7 Rust was materially faster than the Phase 1 Python median (4.865 s vs 5.857 s) while using the production lock/tempfile/rename write path.
Rust-backed full-store read-state mutation over the deterministic 5k corpus. Phase 7 Rust was faster than the Phase 1 Python median (71.685 ms vs 79.459 ms).

Correctness-first concurrency anchor for append racing a rewrite on the 5k corpus. The Rust path is intentionally serialized through one sidecar lock and tempfile rename, so Phase 7 treats the slower median as the cost of eliminating truncate-before-lock empty-file/lost-row exposure.

Notification modal dismiss burst anchor over a loaded 5k inbox with production Rust-backed persistence. No Phase 1 Python modal baseline was captured, so this guards the Phase 7 Rust median as an absolute ceiling.
